LESSON: PAINTING AND COLLAGE

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Creating and Executing
Topic 1.2: Painting and Collage
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 15

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Painting and Collage, part of Creating and Executing in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six CREATIVE ARTS.

Key inquiry question: Why is tonal variation important in painting? 2. How is texture achieved in a painting and collage picture?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify characteristics of collage,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Painting and Collage in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. classify colour categories on the colour wheel for familiarity,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Painting and Collage in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. paint a still life composition using brush stroke technique,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Painting and Collage in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. create a collage composition for skill acquisition,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Painting and Collage in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. appreciate painting and collage techniques,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Painting and Collage in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify characteristics of collage,

   Painting and Collage helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. classify colour categories on the colour wheel for familiarity,

   Painting and Collage helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. paint a still life composition using brush stroke technique,

   Painting and Collage helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. create a collage composition for skill acquisition,

   Painting and Collage helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. appreciate painting and collage techniques,

   Painting and Collage helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

F. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1.  mix and paint a colour wheel to represent primary, secondary and tertiary colours, Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or use assistive technology.  mix and paint a surface to create tonal gradation by; thinning same tone/adding dark tone,  illustrate painting to create varied texture focusing on; brush position/angle, brush load and brush strokes,  paint any two objects overlapping inspired by 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1.  mix and paint a colour wheel to represent primary, secondary and tertiary colours, Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or use assistive technology.  mix and paint a surface to create tonal gradation by; thinning same tone/adding dark tone,  illustrate painting to create varied texture focusing on; brush position/angle, brush load and brush strokes,  paint any two objects overlapping inspired by 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Painting and Collage together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Critical thinking and problem solving: will be developed as the learner explores multiple perspectives of painting using

varied tools and materials for creativity.

 Digital literacy: The learner uses digital technology to source virtual or actual pictures of players executing skills in football

and painting artwork.

 Creativity and imagination: The learner will apply creative skills in selecting media for painting, and painting the still life

composition.

Values:
 Responsibility: The learner works on art work and clears up after the activities

 Unity: The learner practise tuning the fiddle in turns
